Prices run from 10 to 500 lakhs, mean 254.6, median 253.9, skew 0.01. The histogram is flat (uniform), not right-skewed like real housing prices.

**Q2. Distribution of property sizes**

Sizes run from 500 to 5000 sq ft, mean 2750, median 2747, skew 0.00. Again uniform. A 500 sq ft to 5000 sq ft spread with equal density is a synthetic-data signature.

**Q4. Relationship between size and price**

Correlation is -0.003, i.e. none. In real markets this is one of the strongest relationships. Price here is independent of size, so Price_per_SqFt is driven almost entirely by size (corr -0.61).

Highest: Bangalore (258.5 L), lowest: Cuttack (250.8 L). group means range from 250.8 L to 258.5 L (gap 3.0% of the overall mean: small). Mumbai averages 252.1 L and Silchar 252.6 L, a gap that real markets never show.

**Q8. Median age of properties by locality**

Across 500 localities the median age ranges from 16 to 21 years (overall median 18). Localities are labelled Locality_1..500 and are reused across cities, so a 'locality' is not a real neighbourhood in this data.

**Q9. BHK distribution across cities**

Every city has roughly 20% in each of 1 to 5 BHK (per-cell range 18.6% to 22.0%). No city specialises in any BHK.

**Q10. Price trends for the top 5 most expensive localities**

Top 5: Locality_395, Locality_366, Locality_497, Locality_360, Locality_203 (mean 271 L vs overall 255 L). The dataset has no sale-date column, so a true price-over-time trend is impossible. Price by build period is the closest proxy and it is noisy, with no consistent upward line.
